content.thinking:
The huge online drop with barely-moved offline score on the watched slice really looks like a leak — training data likely overlaps the eval slice, inflating offline metrics without helping online performance. I'm now looking at what the release config actually changed: capacity and mixture stayed at recipe defaults, but lr_scale was altered.

So the plausible mechanism is that lr_scale being bumped to 1.526 amplifies overfitting to whatever leaked training data is inflating the offline score, which would explain why offline looks fine while online generalization collapses.

Since leak isn't a knob I can toggle, the real candidates are capacity, mixture, and lr_scale, and I need to test each via the counterfactual criteria: resetting the true causal knob back to its recipe value on top of the release config should recover online performance, while holding just that knob at its release value on top of the before config should reproduce the regression.

Looking at what actually changed between before and after, only lr_scale moved (1.0 to 1.526) — capacity and mixture stayed fixed at their recipe defaults in both versions. That strongly points to lr_scale as the sole causal knob, since it's the only variable that differs between the two configs; leak, being a data property rather than a config setting, isn't something the release could have directly altered.

So previously lr_scale was 1.0, now it's 1.526 — that's the actual release change. The culprit is lr_scale: pushing it up likely overfits the fine-tune onto the mixture data (which overlaps with eval via the watched-slice leak), tanking online performance while barely touching offline metrics. The fix should revert lr_scale toward its floor of 1.368 and consider retuning capacity/mixture downward to counteract the leak effect.

Now I want to use the lab to test this within a 20-run budget: first confirm the release config reproduces the documented baseline (0.8905 offline, 0.7877 online), then rerun with the pre-release config to isolate lr_scale's contribution.

Since only capacity/mixture changes seem to trigger a retrain-cost multiplier, an lr_scale-only rerun should cost just 1 run. I'll also apply decontamination to release vs before configs to directly test the leak hypothesis, and use the costlier canary check sparingly to see if online performance recovers.
